candidates.title: Compare Meta and Shopify order exports

demandEvidence.chore: Compare manually exported daily ad purchases and Shopify orders to flag dates with possible tracking discrepancies.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: In Shopify, export daily orders for the same 30 days, Online Store channel only, without test and cancelled orders.

ease.reason: The retained steps give an operator-supplied export task, but no supplied source documents a comparison tool.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: a small professional operator may pay for this narrow review; no buying intent or payment is established.

feasibility.reason: A synthetic table comparison fits a small prototype; correct attribution and live exports remain outside scope.

autonomy.reason: A supplied-file flag report can repeat, but the person exports, interprets and investigates every discrepancy.

evidence.reason: The spans specify two 30-day exports and a possible double-count pattern, but this is one instructional post.

experimentPlan.output: A review table that flags dates where supplied ad and store purchase totals differ sharply.
experimentPlan.trigger: After an operator supplies two matching-period CSV files.
steps: Align rows by date using an explicitly chosen date field.
Mark missing dates and unusually large differences without guessing causes.
Produce a review table with both totals and a note for human investigation.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: On a small fictional pair with a known injected mismatch, check that only the expected date is flagged and both input totals are preserved.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: The operator exports and supplies files, confirms comparable attribution settings, decides whether a gap matters, and investigates tracking before changing anything.
unverified: Actual export column names and matching rules
A defensible threshold for unusual differences

candidates.reason: Scored as a bounded supplied-file experiment; below threshold because repeated buyer need and useful discrepancy rules are unverified.

candidates.title: Prepare game test CSV rows for review

demandEvidence.chore: Move mobile game-test CSV observations into a sheet without missing entries or importing the same file twice.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I have tried a Schedule Trigger plus Google Drive Watch Files and also a Webhook from a shortcut on the phone, but the workflow either doesn’t fire at all or fires twice on the same file.

ease.reason: n8n documents CSV extraction and duplicate comparison, though phone intake and sheet writing are not documented here.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: a small professional operator may pay for this narrow review; no buying intent or payment is established.

feasibility.reason: A supplied-file prototype can parse and compare rows; correct identity fields and live trigger behavior remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: CSV parsing and duplicate checks can be automated with documented nodes; a person supplies files and verifies matches.

evidence.reason: The spans describe the current notes-to-CSV-to-Sheets process and failures, but only one operator case.

experimentPlan.output: A review sheet of parsed game-test rows with likely repeat rows marked for a person.
inputs: Fictional CSV rows with battery, temperature, frame-drop and note fields
A proposed stable observation key supplied by the operator
A fictional prior-row set for repeat comparison
experimentPlan.trigger: When an operator manually supplies a completed CSV and a prior-row sample.
steps: Extract CSV records into row objects using the documented n8n extraction node.
Check required sample fields and mark missing values.
Compare rows on an operator-selected key using the documented duplicate-removal capability.
Create a review output that retains original values and labels possible repeats.
Have a person confirm the key and every flagged repeat before sheet entry.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: With a synthetic file containing known complete, incomplete and repeated rows, confirm records are retained and expected repeats are marked without silently deleting observations.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: The operator records or exports the data, chooses a valid stable key, supplies files and reviews every match. This does not repair or prove phone triggers, cloud upload timing, or data persistence.
unverified: Whether the documented duplicate node suits this dataset

candidates.reason: The concrete chore and two attached n8n references support a bounded file-review plan, but the provisional mean is 4.6 and live intake remains unresolved.

candidates.title: Keep received images with reply context

demandEvidence.chore: Pass a received customer image and its message together to an AI step so the agent can identify the pictured product without asking for a resend.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I want the AI agent to recognize that the image has already been received and use the available image to identify the product, rather than asking the customer to resend it.

ease.reason: The request describes two routed inputs, but no supplied reference documents image handoff or image analysis.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small online sellers may pay for fewer repeated image requests; the post proves no buyer intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A synthetic handoff mock is possible, but the core image recognition and Make route behavior are unsupported.

autonomy.reason: A draft product guess would need customer-context checks; image delivery and reliable recognition are undocumented.

evidence.reason: The retained post gives a specific text-plus-image failure, but no frequency, solution or corroboration.

experimentPlan.output: A review card pairing a fictional customer message with its already supplied image reference and a proposed product guess.
experimentPlan.trigger: When a test message includes a sample image and product-identification request.
steps: Keep the message and supplied image reference in one proposed test record.
Compare the sample image against a small labeled fictional catalog.
Draft one possible catalog match with a confidence note.
Show the text, image reference and draft together for human review.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For labeled sample images, check whether the displayed draft points to the known catalog item and never claims certainty when no match is clear.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person authorizes image use, verifies the product match and handles the customer reply; this does not establish a Make integration or safe production image processing.
unverified: Image input support and recognition quality
Whether text and image remain paired through the proposed flow

candidates.reason: The stated failure supports a narrow mock, but the core image handling is unsupported and the provisional mean is 4.0.

candidates.title: Review duplicate rows after missed n8n runs

demandEvidence.chore: Review records created after a missed schedule trigger and identify possible duplicate entries before a person acts on them.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Missed schedule triggers can duplicate everything.

ease.reason: The retained lines mention duplicate risk but give no data format or supplied capability reference for this workflow.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small workflow operators might pay for safer recovery review, but no buyer or purchase evidence appears.

feasibility.reason: A fictional before-and-after row comparison is possible; the trigger and duplicate contract are not specified.

autonomy.reason: A report could mark suspected repeats, but recovery and deletion require human judgment; no workflow support is supplied.

evidence.reason: A maker post states a duplicate risk, without a concrete affected record, frequency or customer request.

experimentPlan.output: A review list marking possible repeat records in a fictional post-run dataset.
inputs: Fictional records before and after a missed schedule
Expected repeat examples for a mock check
experimentPlan.trigger: After an operator supplies two fictional record sets from before and after a schedule interruption.
steps: Compare records using an explicitly supplied identifier.
Mark exact identifier repeats and missing identifiers separately.
Preserve both original rows with review labels.
Ask a person to decide whether a row is a legitimate repeat or a distinct event.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Check a small fixture containing known exact repeats and distinct rows, confirming the report flags only the chosen identifier matches and preserves source rows.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person supplies records, selects the identifier, investigates context and authorizes any correction; the proposal does not prevent missed triggers or repair a live workflow.

candidates.reason: This concrete operational concern is assessed separately, but the proposed review overlaps the game-test duplicate-check workflow in this batch; it is excluded for shared workflow, and its evidence is also too thin for threshold.
